guidelines.fragment_description: A Class can contain attributes and operations. This fragment includes all features that are considered part of the class's definition.
An Attribute is a defining property of a Class, specifying a named slot within which a value of a specified type may be stored.
An Operation is a behavioral feature of a Class that represents a functional service or computation.
An Association represents a relationship between two classes, indicating that objects of one class are connected to objects of another class.
Generalization is a relationship that indicates that one Class inherits from another Class, showing a hierarchy between the two.
A Dependency indicates that a change in one class may affect another class, reflecting a usage or implementation relationship.
Aggregation is a type of association that indicates a whole-part relationship between two classes.
Composition is a strong form of aggregation signifying a whole-part relationship, where the part is existentially dependent on the whole.
